title: SkyTrain Overnight Testing: Hours, Noise and Purpose

evidence.demandEvidence: TransLink began a five-month overnight program on October 3 that can create recurring noise questions for residents near rotating Expo and Millennium line sections.
evidence.readerImpact: Residents can identify the three confirmed overnight windows, understand the two stated noise-reduction measures, and avoid mistaking empty trains for added passenger service.

sourceCaptures.title: SkyTrain begins overnight testing ahead of major network expansion
excerpts: Starting Oct. 3, SkyTrain cars will run overnight on weekends and some Mondays for approximately five months, to prepare for major network expansions.
Over the next five months, all types of SkyTrain cars will undergo overnight testing on sections of the Expo and Millennium lines.
Testing will take place outside regular service hours, with no customers aboard and no disruptions or reductions to regular SkyTrain service.

Test trains will operate in different sections of the Expo and Millennium lines over approximately five months, during the following overnight hours: Saturdays from 1:45 to 5:45 a.m.; Sundays from 1:45 to 6:45 a.m.; Mondays from 12:45 to 4:45 a.m.
The testing will prepare TransLink's new, state-of-the-art, 40,000-square-foot Operations Control Centre to manage SkyTrain service as the network expands.
During testing, the new centre will gradually take control of trains and test a range of operations, including regular daily service, routine maintenance, and emergency response.
This marks the first expansion of SkyTrain's operations control space since 1985, despite the network growing to approximately four times its original size.
Residents near the affected sections of the Expo and Millennium lines may hear trains operating along the guideway during hours when they would not normally be running.
Testing will rotate between locations across Metro Vancouver, rather than taking place in the same area every night. Alarms and announcements will also be suspended wherever possible to reduce noise.

sourceCaptures.title: The future of SkyTrain: A sneak peek at our new Operations Control Centre
excerpts: If you've ridden the SkyTrain past Edmonds Station in Burnaby recently, you may have noticed a mysterious-looking building wrapped in stainless steel.
That's why we're building a new state-of-the-art Operations Control Centre, near SkyTrain's primary Operations and Maintenance Centre.
This new facility is critical to operating the Millennium and Expo Line extensions (the Broadway Subway and Surrey Langley SkyTrain).

sourceCaptures.title: Project Overview - Surrey Langley SkyTrain
excerpts: Named the Dave Barrett Extension, it includes eight stations and three transit exchanges.
The current anticipated in-service date is late 2029.
